# The Hunter's Moon and the God Who Pursues

## Scripture
*"Suppose one of you has a hundred sheep and loses one of them. Doesn't he leave the ninety-nine in the open country and go after the lost sheep until he finds it?"* — Luke 15:4 (NIV)

## Reflection
October's full moon rises fat and golden—what farmers call the Hunter's Moon. For centuries, its brilliant light allowed hunters to pursue their quarry long after sunset. The name itself speaks of pursuit.

There's something in that image that echoes the heart of God.

We often think of faith as our search for God—our reaching upward, our seeking. And there is truth in that. But the deeper truth of the gospel is this: God is the hunter, and we are the pursued. We did not find God; God found us. We did not choose Him first; He chose us. Like a shepherd scanning the hillside under moonlight, He does not wait for the lost to wander home. He comes after us.

Perhaps tonight you feel far off—lost in the shadows of doubt, distraction, or failure. The Hunter's Moon reminds us that the darkness is no obstacle to the One who seeks us. His light pierces the night. His pursuit never tires.

The God of the universe is not distant and disinterested. He is a seeking God, a pursuing Father, a Shepherd who counts His sheep and notices the missing one. And He will not stop until He brings you home.

## Prayer
Father, thank You for not waiting for me to find my way back. Thank You for pursuing me through every dark season. When I feel lost, remind me that Your light still searches, Your love still follows. Draw me home again. Amen.
